currentContext.expansion: Shreyans Papers unit implemented technical upgradations and modernization in the previous year, improving machine runnability, process stability, and capacity utilization. As part of ongoing capex, the Company is installing a Synchro Cutter Machine (Pasaban make) scheduled for commissioning in FY 2026–27, aimed at precise sheet cutting, improved bundle quality, reduced process losses, and enhanced finishing efficiency. Shree Rishabh Papers unit commissioned and stabilized complete automation in Stock Preparation, two Twin Roll Presses in the Pulp mill, and a Bundle Shrink Wrap machine during the year, optimizing chemical costs and improving pulp/paper quality and packaging aesthetics. The unit is also setting up a husk-fired/multi-fuel steam boiler of 42 TPH as a standby to ensure production continuity during primary boiler breakdown/maintenance. The Company remains committed to strategic investments for de-bottlenecking, enhancing production capacity and quality, improving productivity, and reducing manufacturing costs for sustainable long-term growth.

risks.risk: Margin erosion from input cost volatility and lower sales prices
risks.note: Unusually high raw material, fuel, and other input costs in India, combined with significant decreases in sales prices, severely compressed margins and caused financial performance to fall far below expectations.

risks.risk: Unabated imports of paper at lower prices
risks.note: Imports of paper at lower prices persisted throughout the year, depressing revenue and margins despite normal demand volumes.

US tariffs, the Iran-Israel-USA conflict, and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Palestine conflicts created cumulative economic and geopolitical effects that adversely impacted trade and input costs.

risks.risk: Concentrated exposure to writing and printing paper segment
risks.note: The company operates primarily in the writing and printing paper segment, which is growing at only 2-3% annually, making it vulnerable to demand shifts and substitution risks such as digital device adoption in education.

risks.risk: Regulatory and substitution risk from plastic bans and digital adoption
risks.note: While plastic packaging bans may boost packaging paper demand, the company's core segment faces potential demand erosion if digital device bans in classrooms are reversed or if digital substitution accelerates.

risks.risk: Low per capita paper consumption in India
risks.note: India's per capita paper consumption of 15-16 kg is significantly below the global average of 56-57 kg, indicating structural demand uncertainty and dependence on literacy and manufacturing growth drivers.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Shreyans Papers unit implemented technical upgradations and modernization in the previous year, improving machine runnability, process stability, and capacity utilization. As part of ongoing capex, the Company is installing a Synchro Cutter Machine (Pasaban make) scheduled for commissioning in FY 2026–27, aimed at precise sheet cutting, improved bundle quality, reduced process losses, and enhanced finishing efficiency. Shree Rishabh Papers unit commissioned and stabilized complete automation in Stock Preparation, two Twin Roll Presses in the Pulp mill, and a Bundle Shrink Wrap machine during the year, optimizing chemical costs and improving pulp/paper quality and packaging aesthetics. The unit is also setting up a husk-fired/multi-fuel steam boiler of 42 TPH as a standby to ensure production continuity during primary boiler breakdown/maintenance. The Company remains committed to strategic investments for de-bottlenecking, enhancing production capacity and quality, improving productivity, and reducing manufacturing costs for sustainable long-term growth.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established position among leading agro-based writing & printing paper players in India
- Successful technical upgradations and modernization improving machine runnability, process stability, and capacity utilization
- Integrated cost optimization focus through chemical cost reduction, preventive maintenance, and efficient resource management
- Long-standing community and CSR presence (over 31 years) building local stakeholder relationships

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Margin erosion from input cost volatility and lower sales prices — Unusually high raw material, fuel, and other input costs in India, combined with significant decreases in sales prices, severely compressed margins and caused financial performance to fall far below expectations.
- Unabated imports of paper at lower prices — Imports of paper at lower prices persisted throughout the year, depressing revenue and margins despite normal demand volumes.
- Global geopolitical and trade uncertainty — US tariffs, the Iran-Israel-USA conflict, and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Palestine conflicts created cumulative economic and geopolitical effects that adversely impacted trade and input costs.
- Concentrated exposure to writing and printing paper segment — The company operates primarily in the writing and printing paper segment, which is growing at only 2-3% annually, making it vulnerable to demand shifts and substitution risks such as digital device adoption in education.
- Regulatory and substitution risk from plastic bans and digital adoption — While plastic packaging bans may boost packaging paper demand, the company's core segment faces potential demand erosion if digital device bans in classrooms are reversed or if digital substitution accelerates.
- Low per capita paper consumption in India — India's per capita paper consumption of 15-16 kg is significantly below the global average of 56-57 kg, indicating structural demand uncertainty and dependence on literacy and manufacturing growth drivers.
